One-time setup for the Scan now button
  1. Open GitHub → new fine-grained token.
  2. Name it "scan button", set an expiry (up to 1 year).
  3. Repository access: Only select repositories → breakout-scanner.
  4. Permissions → Repository → Actions: Read and write. Nothing else.
  5. Generate, copy the token, paste it here and tap Save.

The token stays in this browser only. It can do nothing except start and read runs of this one repository. Without it, the buttons open GitHub's Run page instead.

Market stanceCautious

Narrow or shaky market. Trade only the strongest setups, at half size, and take profits sooner.

Market review

  • Indexes. The S&P 500 fell 1.9% and is -3.1% over the past month, below its 50-day average (mixed). Small caps led over the month (Nasdaq-100 -6.8%, Russell 2000 +0.9%).
  • Breadth. Participation is narrow: 38% of US stocks are above their 50-day average and 37% above their 200-day. 83 new 52-week highs vs 582 new lows; 23% of stocks advanced, carrying 17% of the dollar volume. Over 10 days, new highs minus new lows average -202 a day and 46% of dollar volume went into rising stocks. 8 distribution days in the last 25 sessions point to institutional selling.
  • Risk. Volatility is elevated: VIX 22.9 (+3.6). The US 10-year yield is 5.12% (+26 bp this week). USD/CAD 1.4303. Credit markets are calm (high-yield bonds holding up against Treasuries).
  • Metals. Gold/silver ratio 82 (rising over the month); gold is leading silver. Real yields are rising (TIPS -0.8% over the month), a headwind for precious metals. Seasonally, September-February is metals' strongest stretch.
  • Sectors. Leading over the month: Health Care (+6.3%) and Consumer Staples (+5.7%). Lagging: Technology (-10.2%) and Energy (-6.7%).
  • Canada. The TSX 60 is -1.0% on the day and -0.3% over the month (uptrend); 52% of TSX stocks are above their 50-day average, with Utilities leading.
  • Scanner. 11 breakouts passed every hard rule today; see the scores below.

The North West Company Inc. Grocery Stores · Consumer Defensive · Canada

The North West Company Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the retail of food and everyday products and services in northern Canada, rural Alaska, the South Pacific, and the Caribbean.

More about the company

The North West Company Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the retail of food and everyday products and services in northern Canada, rural Alaska, the South Pacific, and the Caribbean. The company operates Northern stores, which offers food, general merchandise, and financial services that include cheque cashing, ATMs, and prepaid card products; NorthMart stores that provides fresh food, apparel, and health products and services; and Quickstop convenience stores that provides ready-to-eat food products, fuel, and related services. It also operates Giant Tiger junior discount stores, which offers family fashion, household products, and food products; Valu Lots discount center and direct-to-customer food distribution outlets for remote communities; solo market, a full service grocery; Pharmacy and Convenience stores; and NWC Motorsports, a dealership that offers sales, service, parts and accessories for Ski-doo, Honda, Can-am and other premier brands. In addition, the company also engages in distribution of produces and fresh meats; provides contract tele-pharmacist services; and engages in shipping services. Further, it operates Alaska Commercial Company stores that provides food and general merchandise to remote and rural regions; Pacific Alaska wholesale, a distributor to independent grocery stores, commercial accounts, and individual households; Riteway food markets; and Cost-U-Less mid-size warehouse stores. Additionally, the company also offers gasoline. The North West Company Inc. was formerly known as North West Company Fund and changed its name to The North West Company Inc. in January 2011. The North West Company Inc. was founded in 1668 and is headquartered in Winnipeg, Canada. Company website

Saputo Inc. Packaged Foods · Consumer Defensive · Canada

Saputo Inc. produces, markets, and distributes dairy products in Canada, the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom.

More about the company

Saputo Inc. produces, markets, and distributes dairy products in Canada, the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom. The company offers mozzarella and cheddar; specialty cheeses, such as ricotta, provolone, parmesan, goat cheese, feta, havarti, snacking, romano, string, blue, and soft and processed cheeses; and brie, camembert, brick, colby, farmer, munster, monterey jack, and fresh curd. It also provides fluid milk, cream, yogurt, sour cream, cottage cheese, and ice cream mixes; and butter and butter blends, flavored cream, dips, half and half, whipping cream, value-added beverages, creamers, coffee beverages, aerosol whipped toppings, almond and oat milk, and aseptic food products and beverages. In addition, the company offers dairy ingredients, including milk powder, whey powder, lactose, and whey protein concentrates, as well as lactoferrin and infant formula; spreads and oils; demineralized whey, lactose, casein, galacto-oligosaccharides, dairy ingredient blends, and nutritional products; and distributes fine imported cheese to specialty stores, and dairy and non-dairy products manufactured by third parties, as well as dairy alternative products. It serves customers in the retail, foodservice, and industrial markets. The company sells its products under the Saputo, Armstrong, Alexis de Portneuf, Bari, Cogruet, DuVillage 1860, Kingsey, Shepherd Gourmet Dairy, Stella, Woolwich Goat Dairy, Dairyland, Neilson, Nutrilait, Baxter, Scotsburn, Trutaste, Milk2Go/Lait's Go, Baileys, Heluva Good, Black Creek, Frigo, Frigo Cheese Heads, Lugano, Montchevre, Mozzeria, Saputo Gold, Treasure Cave, DairyStar, Friendship Dairies, Caboolture, CHEER, Cracker Barrel, Devondale, Great Ocean Road, Liddells, Mersey Valley, Mil Lel, Murray Goulburn Ingredients, Sungold, Tasmanian Heritage, Cathedral City, Clover, Country Life, Davidstow, Frylight, Wensleydale Creamery, Vitalite, and Sheese brands. Saputo Inc. was founded in 1954 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada. Company website

What the labels mean

  • Buy Breakout confirmed and it passes the scorecard (70+/100, reward:risk 2+, no earnings within 5 sessions, under 4 warnings). Entry plan below.
  • Watch Breakout not confirmed yet, or it held but doesn't pass the scorecard. Not a buy yet.
  • Don't chase Breakout held but price ran too far above the breakout level. Wait for a pullback.
  • Hold You own it (if you took the Buy). Keep the stop order in place.
  • Take profit Target hit. Sell part, protect the rest.
  • Hold - trailing Holding the remainder with a stop that rises with the price.
  • Sell Exit the position (or your stop order already did).
  • Drop Setup failed or never qualified before entry. Remove from watchlist.

Entry, stop and target are calculated from the breakout level. Profit/loss is measured from the close on the day of the Buy signal; your real entry is the next open. A Buy is exited early if it closes back below the breakout level within 10 sessions (failed breakout).

The score is a pass mark, not a ranking: in the 2022-26 backtest, setups scoring 70-74 did as well as or better than those scoring 75+. Position size risks 1% of the account per trade, so a run of 20 losses (Douglas's sample size) would cost about 18%.
